tytul: How to Use MindSync: Your First Week, Step by Step
tresc_html:
You installed MindSync on a Tuesday, your session is at six, and the app has just greeted you with eight colored tiles under a wide one called Your first week, and a plan that wants you to answer Orca's question. Where do you even start? Record something? Rate something? Open all eight tiles at once, advent-calendar style, and hope for the best?

What MindSync is for (and what it is not)

MindSync is a mobile app that helps people in therapy keep more from every session. Orca is MindSync's AI therapy assistant for the days between sessions, and neither of them is a therapist or a substitute for treatment. The app was built by someone who spent 10 years and around $130,000 on therapy and kept forgetting what happened in it, and a licensed psychologist is on the team (more on who MindSync is built for).

Get it on the App Store or Google Play (here's what the free trial includes). If you used it before, read [LINK-LATER: whats-new-in-mindsync | everything that changed in the latest update].

Why small steps between sessions matter:

In 2003, Roy Kessels reviewed what patients remember from medical appointments in the Journal of the Royal Society of Medicine: 40% to 80% of what a practitioner says is forgotten immediately, and almost half of what people do remember is wrong. In 2010, Kazantzis, Whittington and Dattilio pooled 46 studies with 1,072 people in Clinical Psychology: Science and Practice, and in the controlled ones, therapy with homework beat the same therapy without it (d = 0.48). A moderate effect, earned on days nobody was watching.

Kessels studied medical visits, not therapy, and the homework studies weren't about apps, so none of this proves an app makes therapy work. Both do suggest the days between sessions count.

Day one: setup and your first talk with Orca

Setup covers what you want to keep an eye on, how strong each one feels from 1 to 10, your therapy and next session, what to call Orca and how it should talk to you. Resist ticking every box. Two or three areas that match what you talk about in therapy will still be there in month two, while ten turn every check-in into a small tax return. You can add, archive or remove them later on the Focus Areas tile.

Next you meet Orca, which isn't a therapist and doesn't replace yours. The first talk takes about three minutes, by voice or in writing: Orca asks three short questions, then the conversation is yours until you end it. You can also skip it for now. What Orca heard is saved in Reflect, and your first Before therapy card starts from it. Orca keeps short notes to remember you, which you can read or delete in Settings under What Orca remembers. Before you share much, read what happens to what you tell an AI.

A few more screens later you're on Main, about ten minutes in, and you haven't written a paragraph.

The eight steps of Your first week:

If you're in therapy, the wide tile opens this plan:

  1. Set up your account (Setup, 3 min). Done before you see the plan.
  2. Answer Orca's question (Reflect, 3 min). One question, answered in a short talk.
  3. Add your next session (Next therapy session, 1 min). Done already if you gave a date in setup.
  4. Leave a voice note (Between Sessions, 1 min). Say how the week is going.
  5. Quick check-in (Focus Areas, 30 sec). One rating means nothing yet. It's the first dot.
  6. Save one thing for therapy (Therapy Agenda, 1 min). A question or topic for next time.
  7. Keep a small habit (Habits, 1 min). Check one off, or add one.
  8. Your first week (Weekly recap, 2 min read). A look back, and a rhythm for what's next.

If you're not in therapy right now, or chose not to personalize MindSync to your therapy in setup, step 3 is Talk with Orca again and step 6 is Save a question for later.

None of the steps has a day. Each counts as soon as you do it, in any order, and the plan points you to the next open one, with an optional daily nudge. Step 8 opens on day seven, or once the first seven are done. After all eight, the tile leaves Main. Older accounts don't get the plan.

It's short on purpose. Week one is when apps get moved to a folder called Misc on your third home screen.

[FEATURE: first-week-plan | Eight small steps on Main, a few minutes each, none of them tied to a day.]

Around your first session: before, during, after

The + button, on every tab except Reflect, opens After Therapy, Prepare for Therapy, Between Sessions and Record Session. The session tile on Main shows Prepare your notes in the days before and After therapy once it's over.

Before: the Before therapy card

Open Prepare for Therapy a day or an hour before. You get a short summary and up to three numbered questions to bring, with to-dos, threads, patterns and Focus Areas added once there's enough to show. If you had your first talk with Orca, the first card starts from it, so it's thin but not empty. Add the thing you keep circling back to. There's also a guide on how to prepare for a therapy session when your mind goes blank.

During: recording (and asking your therapist first)

Ask before you press anything: "I'm trying an app that records sessions so I stop forgetting what we talked about. Would that be okay with you?" Laws differ between countries and US states, and some require everyone's consent. As a practical rule (not legal advice), you don't record without your therapist's yes, and they're free to say no. Before your first recording, MindSync asks you to confirm they agreed.

If they say yes, tap Record Session as you start (sessions under 10 minutes aren't processed). You get a summary card with to-dos, threads, realizations and the questions your therapist asked, which are usually the first thing to go by Thursday.

[FEATURE: session-recording | With your therapist's okay, get a summary card with the questions they asked you.]

After: the After therapy card while it's fresh

Open After Therapy before you get back to your day: what landed, what you agreed to try, what you avoided saying. Five minutes in the car beats 40 minutes on Sunday, when the session has blurred into a vague sense that something helpful happened. The blur isn't a personal failing, and here's why you forget most of what your therapist says.

After three sessions, the card adds Your progress in therapy: a short phrase like Getting steadier or A harder stretch, drawn from your own Focus Areas, notes and recordings. It isn't a score, a verdict on your mental health or a review of your therapist (see what a progress line can and can't tell you, and what to do if you feel worse after a session).

The week between sessions

When something happens, tap +, choose Between Sessions and say it out loud, unedited. Read the transcript back, accept it, and it waits for your next prep. The note you record in a stairwell exists. The paragraph you plan to write tonight doesn't (more on why talking beats typing for most people).

To-dos from your therapist and from Orca wait on the To-do tile, as a job for today instead of a guilty thought in the waiting room. Topics for next time go on the Therapy Agenda tile, and Workspace holds it all in a fixed order. For weeks that get away from you, there's getting therapy homework done when the week eats it.

The Habits tile shows the last seven days, so you can still check off a day you missed. To think something through, talk with Orca in Reflect, in writing or, on Premium, by voice. The rest of the routine is in a weekly system that fits real life.

What shows up after a week or two:

Week one is mostly input. The last step sums it up: what you did, where things stand compared with setup and what Orca noticed, plus a suggested rhythm you can keep or swap for your own.

The Focus Areas tile charts your last 14 ratings and puts the trend into words. Weekly summaries land in Timeline, with filters at the top for the day your therapist asks when something started. Character's strengths, like Courage, grow from moments in what you share, never from just opening the app.

Two weeks of ratings is a hint, not proof. One bad week isn't a verdict on your therapy, and no app can tell you what caused what. What it can do is stop the conversation running on memory alone. Two more reads: why mood tracking stops working after two weeks and how your data is stored and who can see it.

This is what MindSync's first-week plan is for. Log the question you didn't get to, the voice note from the stairwell, the habit you kept on a bad day. Give it time, and Main and your After therapy cards turn those entries into something you can see: what's waiting today, how your Focus Areas are moving and, after three sessions, your progress line. Then walk into your next session already past "so, where were we?"

Which of the eight steps do you already know you'll put off, and what would make it a one-minute job?

[FEATURES: What to set up in the first week || session-prep | The first minutes of your session go to what matters instead of a recap. || session-debrief | Your takeaways while they're fresh, and a progress line after three sessions. || voice-notes | The thing you'd forget by Friday, said out loud on Tuesday and waiting in text.]

Frequently asked questions

What is MindSync used for?

MindSync is used to keep more from therapy. You prepare with a Before therapy card, note what you took away on an After therapy card, record sessions with your therapist's permission to get a summary card, and add voice notes and Focus Areas check-ins in between. Orca, MindSync's AI therapy assistant for the days between sessions, asks questions in Reflect but isn't a therapist. MindSync supports therapy and doesn't replace it.

Is MindSync free?

MindSync starts with four days of Premium for free, and nothing is charged automatically. After that, the Free plan keeps a limited number of Before and After therapy cards, notes and Reflect messages each month, plus a small number of session recordings in total. Premium removes the limits and adds voice talks with Orca. Current prices are on the membership page.

Can I record my therapy session with MindSync?

Yes, MindSync can record a therapy session if your therapist agrees, and you ask before the session rather than halfway through it. The app asks you to confirm that consent before your first recording, and sessions shorter than 10 minutes aren't processed. Recording rules vary between countries and US states, and some require everyone's consent. If your therapist says no, the After therapy card captures most of the same material from your side.

Does MindSync work without a therapist?

Partly. Most of MindSync works without a therapist, but the session tools don't. Focus Areas check-ins, voice notes, Reflect with Orca, Habits and Character all work on their own, and some people use them while they wait for a therapist to have an opening. If you're not in therapy, the first-week plan swaps two steps for ones that don't need a session. The Before and After therapy cards and recording only make sense with a therapist.

Do I have to journal every day for it to be useful?

No, MindSync doesn't need daily journaling. The daily part is an optional Focus Areas check-in, which takes about 30 seconds. Notes are for when something happens, and in most weeks that's two or three moments rather than seven. The first-week steps have no set days, Habits lets you check off a day you missed, and missing days don't break anything.
